clean_source_blocks.text: A running look — in reverse chronological order — at the bigger tech companies that have announced significant layoffs this year with AI as a stated factor.

It's 2026 and the year is just getting started, but layoffs are already piling up across multiple industries. Major U.S. companies in tech, finance, retail, logistics, and consumer services have announced job cuts as they reshape operations, reduce costs, and adapt to long-term shifts driven by automation, artificial intelligence, and changing economic conditions. And while these layoffs largely spread into the tech sector, the reach extends into multinational e-commerce companies and retail giants. Here's a running list of 2026 layoffs at major companies across the U.S., including the latest announcement that a tax giant is axing 17% of its workforce. This list will be updated as more companies announce layoffs in 2026.

Angi, the contractor listing platform formerly known as Angie's List, announced plans to cut around 350 jobs in January. The company said the layoffs are intended to reduce operating expenses and optimize its organizational structure for long-term growth. Angi also cited efficiency gains driven by artificial intelligence as a contributing factor. In a regulatory filing, the company estimated the cuts could save up to $80 million annually. Block (the company that owns Square and Cash App) is laying off more than 4,000 employees — roughly 40% of its workforce — as CEO Jack Dorsey moves to reshape the fintech company around artificial intelligence. In a letter to shareholders, Dorsey said "intelligence tools have changed what it means to build and run a company," adding that a smaller team using AI can operate more efficiently.

Oracle disclosed Monday that it has reduced its workforce by 21,000 employees over the past 12 months, a decline of 13%, which means more cuts than was previously known, including jobs eliminated because of AI. “The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,” the company said in an annual financial regulatory filing. The revelation puts new numbers to what feels to many in the tech industry like an epidemic: companies reporting record revenues while simultaneously culling their workforces, pointing to AI as both the engine of growth and the reason for the cuts. Tech layoffs hit their highest single month in years in May, and AI was the most-cited reason, according to outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas. ---

Tech layoffs hit their highest single month in years in May, and AI was the most-cited reason, according to outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

[Lähde: Tech Times]
As of June 14, 2026, 247 layoff events have displaced 183,966 workers across the tech, finance, and healthcare sectors — an average of 1,115 jobs lost every working day, nearly double the 564-per-day pace recorded in 2025. The month of May alone accounted for roughly 40,000 cuts, the highest single month in two years, according to TechCrunch. And almost everywhere, one explanation keeps surfacing: artificial intelligence.

The question increasingly being asked by laid-off employees, labor economists, and even a few CEOs is whether that explanation is actually true — or whether AI has simply become the most defensible thing to say when you need to trim payroll.

What makes 2026 structurally different from prior downturns is how openly executives are naming AI as the cause. Where companies once hid behind "restructuring" and "efficiency," many now say the quiet part out loud.

Meta is the clearest example. The company cut roughly 8,000 roles in May while redirecting resources toward AI work, even as it prepares to spend over $100 billion in 2026 on data centers and hardware. An internal memo tied the reductions to offsetting the company's AI investment costs. Notably, Meta is not cutting because it is struggling: the company reported strong first-quarter results, with revenue up roughly a third year over year.

The pattern repeats across the industry. payload.title: Tekoäly näkyy yhä useammin suurten teknologiayhtiöiden irtisanomisperusteissa
payload.summary: Useat suuret yhdysvaltalaisyhtiöt ovat tänä vuonna ilmoittaneet merkittävistä henkilöstövähennyksistä ja maininneet tekoälyn yhtenä muutoksia vauhdittavana tekijänä.
payload.content:
Useat suuret yhdysvaltalaiset teknologiayhtiöt ja niitä lähellä olevat yritykset ovat vuonna 2026 ilmoittaneet merkittävistä irtisanomisista, joissa tekoäly on mainittu yhtenä perusteena tai toimintaa muuttavana voimana. Taustalla ovat yhtiöiden mukaan kustannusten leikkaukset, organisaatioiden uudistaminen ja automaation sekä tekoälyn mahdollistamat tehokkuushyödyt.

## Irtisanomisia eri toimialoilla

Vuoden 2026 irtisanomisia on kertynyt useilla aloilla, kuten teknologiassa, rahoituksessa, vähittäiskaupassa, logistiikassa ja kuluttajapalveluissa. Yhtiöt ovat perustelleet vähennyksiä muun muassa toimintojen uudelleenjärjestelyllä, kulujen karsimisella ja pitkän aikavälin muutoksilla, joita automaatio, tekoäly ja taloustilanne aiheuttavat.

Teknologiasektorilla tekoäly on noussut erityisen näkyväksi selitykseksi. Kyse ei lähteiden perusteella ole vain yksittäisistä pienistä sopeutuksista, vaan useissa tapauksissa tuhansien tai jopa kymmenientuhansien työpaikkojen vähennyksistä.

## Oracle, Block ja Angi esimerkkeinä

Oracle kertoi vähentäneensä henkilöstöään 21 000 työntekijällä viimeisten 12 kuukauden aikana. Vähennys vastaa 13 prosenttia yhtiön työvoimasta. Yhtiö totesi vuosittaisessa viranomaisraportissaan, että tekoälyteknologioiden käyttöönotto ja soveltaminen sen toiminnoissa ovat johtaneet ja voivat jatkossakin johtaa henkilöstövähennyksiin.

Block, joka omistaa Square- ja Cash App -palvelut, on vähentämässä yli 4 000 työntekijää. Määrä vastaa noin 40 prosenttia sen henkilöstöstä. Toimitusjohtaja Jack Dorsey on kuvannut muutosta osaksi yhtiön rakentamista tekoälyn ympärille ja arvioinut, että pienempi tiimi voi tekoälyä hyödyntämällä toimia tehokkaammin.

Myös Angi, aiemmin Angie's List -nimellä tunnettu urakoitsijalistausalusta, ilmoitti tammikuussa suunnitelmasta vähentää noin 350 työpaikkaa. Yhtiö sanoi tavoittelevansa alempia toimintakuluja ja pitkän aikavälin kasvua tukevaa organisaatiorakennetta. Se mainitsi myös tekoälyn tuomat tehokkuushyödyt yhtenä vaikuttavana tekijänä ja arvioi säästöjen voivan nousta enintään 80 miljoonaan dollariin vuodessa.

## Tekoäly on sekä kasvu- että leikkausperuste

Irtisanomiset kuvaavat laajempaa jännitettä teknologiayhtiöissä: tekoälyä esitellään samaan aikaan kasvun moottorina ja perusteena työvoiman supistamiselle. Uudelleensijoitusyhtiö Challenger, Gray & Christmasin mukaan teknologia-alan irtisanomiset nousivat toukokuussa korkeimmalle kuukausitasolle vuosiin, ja tekoäly oli yleisimmin mainittu syy.
summary_bullets: Useat suuret yhdysvaltalaisyhtiöt ovat vuonna 2026 maininneet tekoälyn henkilöstövähennysten yhteydessä.
Oracle kertoi vähentäneensä 21 000 työntekijää 12 kuukaudessa, ja Block on leikkaamassa yli 4 000 työpaikkaa.
Angi suunnittelee noin 350 työpaikan vähennystä ja arvioi säästöjen voivan nousta enintään 80 miljoonaan dollariin vuodessa.

A running look — in reverse chronological order — at the bigger tech companies that have announced significant layoffs this year with AI as a stated factor.

It's 2026 and the year is just getting started, but layoffs are already piling up across multiple industries. Major U.S. companies in tech, finance, retail, logistics, and consumer services have announced job cuts as they reshape operations, reduce costs, and adapt to long-term shifts driven by automation, artificial intelligence, and changing economic conditions. And while these layoffs largely spread into the tech sector, the reach extends into multinational e-commerce companies and retail giants. Here's a running list of 2026 layoffs at major companies across the U.S., including the latest announcement that a tax giant is axing 17% of its workforce. This list will be updated as more companies announce layoffs in 2026.

Angi, the contractor listing platform formerly known as Angie's List, announced plans to cut around 350 jobs in January. The company said the layoffs are intended to reduce operating expenses and optimize its organizational structure for long-term growth. Angi also cited efficiency gains driven by artificial intelligence as a contributing factor. In a regulatory filing, the company estimated the cuts could save up to $80 million annually. Block (the company that owns Square and Cash App) is laying off more than 4,000 employees — roughly 40% of its workforce — as CEO Jack Dorsey moves to reshape the fintech company around artificial intelligence. In a letter to shareholders, Dorsey said "intelligence tools have changed what it means to build and run a company," adding that a smaller team using AI can operate more efficiently.

Oracle disclosed Monday that it has reduced its workforce by 21,000 employees over the past 12 months, a decline of 13%, which means more cuts than was previously known, including jobs eliminated because of AI. “The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,” the company said in an annual financial regulatory filing. The revelation puts new numbers to what feels to many in the tech industry like an epidemic: companies reporting record revenues while simultaneously culling their workforces, pointing to AI as both the engine of growth and the reason for the cuts. Tech layoffs hit their highest single month in years in May, and AI was the most-cited reason, according to outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas. ---
